title: PossibleCooker Beef and Potato Picadillo with Tomato Gravy
description: Lean beef and tender potatoes simmer together and are finished with a smooth caramelized-onion and tomato gravy.

ingredients.name: low-sodium beef broth
ingredients.note: Choose plain meat-and-bone broth without a vegetable blend.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: Keep warm and use only as needed.

steps.title: Caramelize the onion
steps.text: Cook {onion} in {oil} in the HexClad over medium-low for 18–25 minutes, stirring often and adding small splashes of {topup} as needed, until entirely soft and deep golden.

steps.title: Start the potatoes
steps.text: Meanwhile place {potatoes} and three quarters of {broth} in the PossibleCooker. Bring to a simmer on Sear/Sauté HIGH with the lid off, then cook for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer the beef
steps.text: Pinch {beef} into small loose pieces and lower them into the potato broth. Restore the simmer, switch to Sear/Sauté LOW and cook uncovered for 10–16 minutes. Break up large clusters as they cook. Check a thick piece for 160°F and a potato cube for fork tenderness.

steps.title: Puree the tomato base
steps.text: Blend the caramelized onion with {tomato}, the reserved {broth}, {cumin} and {oregano} until smooth. Return the puree to the HexClad.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Make the tomato gravy
steps.text: Ladle the cooking liquid from the beef into the HexClad. Bring the combined sauce to a full boil, stir in the slurry and simmer for 1 minute until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Combine the picadillo
steps.text: Turn the cooker off. Fold the finished gravy through the moist beef and potatoes, crushing a few cubes against the pot, and ladle into bowls.

notes: Make ahead: Caramelize and puree the onion a day ahead; refrigerate it with the tomato base. Option A uses smooth tomato puree. For gentler Option B, replace it in equal measure with plain, peeled roasted sweet bell pepper puree and reduce the cumin. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the beef and gravy for up to 2 months. The small potato pieces may soften further and can be mashed into the sauce. Fridge reheat: Warm a single portion with its sauce in a covered HexClad skillet over medium-low, adding a splash of water if thick. Stir or turn gently and begin checking after 5 minutes. Heat the food to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Use the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 314 kcal, 31.2 g protein, 22.8 g total carbohydrate, 10.3 g fat, 2.1 g fiber, 129 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
